title: Bill Doler, the polar bear and the grizzly
summary: Freeman tells of alto player Bill Doler feeding bears at Lincoln Park after hours, his mauled hand, and his golf club revenge.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Now, in this band, I had a close friend, Bill Doler. Bill Doler was a very wild guy and as you know or may not know, in those days, there were bars in Chicago, that were open all night, they never closed. There was a place called the Ohio Inn that was open 24 hours a day and made their political payoffs, of course, and we used to -- we'd get through about four in the morning and we'd go over and have a drink and a little bite to eat or something, and sit around and talk, So we lived near Lincoln Park and now, one Saturday -- Well, let's see, on Saturdays we played over past

midnight into Sunday about 5:00 in the morning. So now we're over in this bar, drinking and suddenly it's starting to get light, it's about 7:00 in the morning, and Bill Doler said, 'Oh, I have a wonderful idea. Let's bring some cheese and nuts and things up and feed the bears, the polar bears come out about this hour.'

So we walked up there and surely enough, there was a polar bear out, so Bill put this food on his hand, put his hand in and the polar bear ate the food off Bill's hand without scratching his hand, but I was scared to death, but in the next cage was the grizzly, a female grizzly and Bill tried it with her and she grabbed his hand and just slit three of his fingers right down, and it was a terrible thing, and I had to walk to the hospital and luckily he was a strong guy and luckily he healed in about six weeks, his hand healed.
But can you imagine, he nearly lost it. He nearly lost three fingers.

Well, anyway, he got drunk again -- he was a golfer-- and he got to thinking about that polar bear -- that grizzly bear, and he wanted to get even. He got his five-iron and he went over, terribly drunk, went over in the morning and when that grizzly bear came out, he hit the grizzly bear over the head and as the grizzly bear was going down, Bill said, 'Do you know, she had a guilty look on her face.'
When you tell these stories, they are so incredible
you don't expect people to believe them, but there they are. There's no reason to make up a story unless it actually happened.
